title: Disjoint pullback of internal module extension by zero vanishes
statement: Let Lambda be any commutative condensed ring, and use internal coefficient modules Mod_{Lambda_T} with Lambda_T=p_T^*Lambda [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let j:U -> X be an open immersion of schemes and let g:W -> X be any scheme morphism whose image is disjoint from the image of j. For every internal module M over Lambda_U, the actual coefficient module pullback g^*(j_!M) is a zero object. Here j_! is the coefficient-linear extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], and g^* is the actual scalar-extension pullback [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. No quasi-compactness, finiteness, Noetherian, or immersion hypothesis on g is needed.

source.place: The assertion that extension by zero restricts to zero on X minus U; generalized to any morphism with image disjoint from U. Existing complete source proof: ModuleObject/OpenClosed.lean, isZero_upperStar_obj_openImmersionLowerShriek_of_disjoint. Compare Stacks proetale.tex Tags 09BN and 09AH and sites-modules.tex Tag 03DI.

proof.text: The coefficient map alpha_g is an isomorphism, so extension of scalars along it is restriction along its inverse. Thus the underlying abelian sheaf of g^*N is canonically g^* of the underlying sheaf of N. The underlying sheaf of j_!M is abelian extension by zero. These are precisely upperStarObjXIso and openImmersionLowerShriek_comp_forget in the existing implementation.

For an abelian sheaf H on W, the open restriction j^*g_*H is zero: over a pro-etale object T over U its sections are H(T times_X W). Disjointness of the two images makes this fibre product empty; the sheaf condition on the empty covering makes its sections zero. The open inverse image is restriction, so this gives the asserted zero sheaf.

The two abelian adjunctions identify Hom(g^*j_!M,H) with Hom(M,j^*g_*H). The latter has one element by the previous step, for every H. Therefore g^*j_!M is initial and hence zero in the abelian category. Combining with the underlying-sheaf comparisons in Step 1 makes the underlying sheaf of the internal module g^*j_!M zero. The module forgetful functor is faithful, so its identity is zero and the internal module is zero. This is the complete existing source theorem, rather than a new unproved statement.

proof_origin.place: Existing source proof via abelian disjoint-image vanishing and the canonical scalar-extension comparison. The node records an already proved source declaration; no Lean declaration or hole is added.

lean.statement: lemma isZero_upperStar_obj_openImmersionLowerShriek_of_disjoint {U W X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (g : W ⟶ X) (hjg : Disjoint (Set.range j.base) (Set.range g.base)) (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology U) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ U)) : IsZero ((g)^*⟦Λ⟧.obj ((j)_!open⟦Λ⟧.obj M))
lean.note: Exact existing source theorem, imported and used by the compiling item proof. Lambda and its commutative monoid structure are section variables. A zero module, empty U or W, the zero coefficient ring, and arbitrary non-Noetherian schemes all satisfy the statement; disjointness is the only geometric vanishing hypothesis. The blueprint search found an etale abelian analogue (lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowershriek), not this pro-etale internal module statement.
